Purdue University teaches GIS coursework, including hands on mapping exercises in which students or instructors add points to OpenStreetMap as part of an assignment. A student or class project point named for the activity itself, rather than for any building or business at that location, is a well documented pattern in OpenStreetMap data, and this entry fits that pattern closely.

No Purdue facilities record, department page, or IT infrastructure document describes a data center at this address, and nothing in the name or location suggests one exists there. This entry is presented here as a likely OpenStreetMap teaching or mapping exercise artifact rather than as a confirmed data center. No capacity, power, or tenancy specifications are published for it because there is no indication a dedicated facility of that kind exists at this point.

reading.body:
"Learning GIS!" is not a data center. It is a mapped point in West Lafayette, Indiana, named for a GIS course exercise rather than a building.

The entry sits at an address on Agricultural Mall in Tippecanoe County and is attributed to Purdue University. The name reads as a class, lab, or student mapping project, and the pattern matches OpenStreetMap teaching artifacts where participants add labeled points as coursework. No operator specification page, facility record, or departmental document describes a data center at this address.

This matters for AI infrastructure accounting because registry rows like this one can inflate facility counts without representing any load. Indiana has six mapped facilities here, and only two publish power figures, totaling 22.5 MW. This entry publishes no megawatts, so it does not belong in any tally of the state's confirmed capacity or its grid impact.

What the data does not tell you is whether a real facility exists at these coordinates under a different name. It only establishes that this row, as named and documented, is not evidence of one.
